method: Approximate visible grid junction centers chosen from saved RGB crop. Compute four-neighbor maximum-bottleneck paths for high and low diagonal probability pairs. Values are diagnostic connection levels, not assumed continuous saddles or guaranteed interval bounds. Interior ports can route around each other; report ordering explicitly and test cutoff intersections only for empirically ordered, separated cases. Sensitivity includes radius 14/18/22, center shifts up to two crop pixels, and alternating corner ports on the patch boundary.
limitations: Approximate visible junction neighborhoods do not certify exact physical contact or hidden cutting geometry.
Connection levels include finite raster/field resolution and port choice; neither ordered cases nor a common cutoff would prove desired physical topology.
Sparse known-material pixel error excludes uncertain edges; it is not full-image accuracy.
This is a diagnostic on previously inspected development photos, not a new independent benchmark.

Known-mask blindness is a property of labels/loss. These photos are held out of the model producing their predictions, so this is not a claim that their own omitted pixels directly caused that particular model output.
findings: Both checker masks exactly reproduce from untouched model probabilities before the template solver; tracing and MILP cannot be the initial cause of those gaps.

256px letterboxed probabilities are bilinearly sampled into a 400px overlap. Upsampling adds no new evidence; the shallow RGB path means encoder stride alone does not establish the cause.

"""Ideal checker control: no learned model, source image or training execution."""
from pathlib import Path
import contextlib,io,json,hashlib
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
 import audit as a
import numpy as np
root=Path.cwd();out=root/'tmp/heart-learning/material-topology-audit-v1';base=json.loads((out/'report.json').read_text());cases=[]
for case in base['cases']:
 centers=[j['cropCenter']for j in case['junctions']];xs=sorted(set(c[0]for c in centers));ys=sorted(set(c[1]for c in centers));h=a.homography(case['cropQuad']);inverse=np.linalg.inv(h);w=np.asarray(case['sourceWindow']);yy,xx=np.mgrid[:256,:256];pix=np.stack([xx,yy],axis=-1);yc,xc=np.mgrid[:400,:400];crop=np.stack([xc+.5,yc+.5],axis=-1);points=a.project(h,crop);fieldpoints=(points-w[:2])*[256/(w[2]-w[0]),256/(w[3]-w[1])]
 expected=(np.searchsorted(xs,crop[...,0],side='right')+np.searchsorted(ys,crop[...,1],side='right'))%2
 native=[a.levels(expected.astype(np.float32),x,y,r=18,inset=0)for x,y in centers]
 controls=[{'kind':'native-400-hard-checker','nativeFieldSupersamplingPerAxis':None,'summary':a.summarize(native),'junctions':native,'maskErrorAgainstSyntheticNative400':0.0}]
 for ss in [1,4,8]:
  field=np.zeros((256,256),dtype=float)
  for sy in range(ss):
   for sx in range(ss):
    source=w[:2]+(pix+[(sx+.5)/ss,(sy+.5)/ss])*(w[2:]-w[:2])/256
    rect=a.project(inverse,source)
    v=(np.searchsorted(xs,rect[...,0],side='right')+np.searchsorted(ys,rect[...,1],side='right'))%2
    field+=v/(ss*ss)
  p=a.sample(field.astype(np.float32),fieldpoints)
  js=[a.levels(p,x,y,r=18,inset=0)for x,y in centers]
  controls.append({'kind':'projected-256-bilinear-400','nativeFieldSupersamplingPerAxis':ss,'summary':a.summarize(js),'junctions':js,'maskErrorAgainstSyntheticNative400':float(np.mean((p>=.5)!=expected))})
 cases.append({'id':case['id'],'controls':controls})
r={'schema':'material-ideal-checker-resampling-control-1','scriptSha256':hashlib.sha256(Path(__file__).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'auditScriptSha256':hashlib.sha256((out/'audit.py').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),'method':'An ideal continuous piecewise-constant checker uses vertical/horizontal boundaries at the approximate photographed grid centers. The checker is projected to the saved 256x256 source window, using fixed 1x1/4x4/8x8 box coverage samples per field pixel; bilinear resampling returns to the saved 400x400 crop. Boundary-corner diagnostic ports use radius18. A direct native400 hard checker is also measured without any resize; integer grid boundaries fall between pixels. No colors, learned model, source photographs, training annotations or solver enter this synthetic control.','limitations':['This tests this particular raster chain, not the camera point-spread function, JPEG, colors, network architecture or actual nonstraight photographed grid.','Approximate photo centers become exact synthetic junctions only in this control. They are not asserted to be exact junction ground truth in the photos.','Coverage averaging is deterministic numerical quadrature, not the exact PIL resizing kernel or an asserted physical camera model.','Native hard checker gives a degenerate diagnostic: both same-color diagonal pairs lack a four-neighbor path (levels0,1), despite exact continuum corner contact. The raster reachability diagnostic is therefore not a topology ground-truth test.'],'cases':cases}
(out/'resampling-control.json').write_text(json.dumps(r,indent=2)+'\n')
for c in cases:
 print(c['id'])
 for v in c['controls']:print(v['kind'],v['nativeFieldSupersamplingPerAxis'],v['summary'],'synthetic mask error',v['maskErrorAgainstSyntheticNative400'])
